prompt: Complete a static paint method that translates and scales the graphics context, draws a 10x10 square in the transformed space, then undoes both transforms before stamping a corner marker.
explanation: translate and scale do not move anything already drawn -- they change the coordinate system used by every later drawing call, so the same fillRect(0, 0, 10, 10) lands somewhere different and comes out a different size. Transforms compose, so scale after translate scales around the translated origin. Undoing them means applying the inverses in reverse order, which is why the scale is undone before the translation.
hints: Paint the background before any transform, while the coordinates still match the image.
After translate(tx, ty) the point (0, 0) is at screen position (tx, ty).
To undo, apply the inverse operations in the opposite order: scale back by 1.0 / factor first, then translate by -tx, -ty.
